{\sffamily\bfseries\LARGE SysML v1 \textrightarrow{} v2 port}\hfill{\sffamily\large quick reference}\par\vspace{3pt}
\hrule height 1.2pt\vspace{4pt}
{\small Two core-Perl tools move a legacy model into SysML v2 text under Git: \cmd{bin/xmi2sysml.pl} reads a Cameo/MagicDraw XMI export
(one \cmd{.sysml} file per top-level package); \cmd{bin/reqif2sysml.pl} reads a DOORS module as ReqIF or CSV (requirements with their
\cmd{doorsId}, and the trace behind metrics C, F, G, I). Offline, Git for Windows only. They give a \emph{starting point}: whatever
cannot be mapped becomes a \cmd{// TODO} line with its \cmd{xmi:id}, never dropped, and a person reviews each segment before it is committed.}\par
\begin{multicols}{2}
\head{The daily loop}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Export} the model from Cameo and the requirements from DOORS into \cmd{exports/}, dated, outside the model repo.
\item \textbf{Read the report before converting:}
\begin{cmds}
perl bin/xmi2sysml.pl --report exports/2026-10-05-legacy.xmi
perl bin/reqif2sysml.pl --report exports/2026-10-05-system.reqif
\end{cmds}
Check three things: the \emph{unmapped} list, \emph{stereotypes not converted}, \emph{type references not resolved}. If one matters, fix the export first.
\item \textbf{Convert into a branch} of the model repo:
\begin{cmds}
git switch -c port/structure
perl ../agile/bin/xmi2sysml.pl --out model --check \textbackslash
\ \ ../exports/2026-10-05-legacy.xmi
perl ../agile/bin/reqif2sysml.pl --out model \textbackslash
\ \ --layout "\_reqs/\{pkg\}.sysml" --check ../exports/...reqif
\end{cmds}
\item \textbf{Review in Git:} \cmd{git status}, \cmd{git diff --stat}, then the diff segment by segment.
\item \textbf{Work the TODOs in Vim:} \cmd{:vimgrep /TODO/ model/**/*.sysml} then \cmd{:copen}; \cmd{:cnext}/\cmd{:cprev}. Each line names the v1 type and \cmd{xmi:id} to find it in Cameo.
\item \textbf{Lint:} \cmd{perl tools/sysml/model.pl lint} at 0 errors / 0 warnings (Vim: \cmd{\textbackslash ml}).
\item \textbf{Commit one segment at a time:} \cmd{git add -p model/structure}; message \cmd{port: structure from legacy.xmi 2026-10-05}; merge through the gate.
\item \textbf{Collect the metrics:} \cmd{perl bin/status-metrics.pl collect ...}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\head{Keep hand edits safe}
The output is deterministic: the same export gives the same bytes. A re-run also \emph{overwrites} your hand edits, so:
\begin{itemize}
\item Once a segment is ported and hand-fixed, \textbf{stop regenerating it}. Convert into \cmd{--out ../scratch} and copy over only the segments still being ported.
\item Use \cmd{--report} to count what remains; its \emph{ported vs remaining} line uses metric A's type filter.
\end{itemize}\end{minipage}
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\head{xmi2sysml options}
{\small\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\ttfamily\footnotesize}l X@{}}
--report & mapping summary: in by \cmd{xmi:type}, ported vs remaining, the TODO list\\
--out DIR & write the files, layout \cmd{\{seg\}/\{pkg\}.sysml}\\
--layout P & another layout, e.g. \cmd{"\{pkg\}.sysml"}\\
--stdout & all files to stdout: \cmd{... | vim -}\\
--req-style & \cmd{usage} (default, what the metrics count) or \cmd{def}\\
--name PKG & package for elements outside any package\\
--check & also run the SysML v2 grammar checker\\
\end{tabularx}}
\end{minipage}
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\head{reqif2sysml options}
{\small\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\ttfamily\footnotesize}l X@{}}
--report & requirements, verification methods, headings, links\\
--model DIR & with \cmd{--report}: trace C, F, G, I against the v2 text, with the ids\\
--id-prefix P & put back the module prefix DOORS drops (\cmd{SYS-})\\
--id-attr N & the id is in another attribute\\
--vm-attr N & the verification-method attribute\\
--attr N & copy a DOORS attribute onto each requirement\\
--csv, --col & CSV input; \cmd{--col id="ID" --col text="Requirement"}\\
\end{tabularx}}
\end{minipage}
\vspace{3pt}{\small\textbf{Exit codes} (both): \cmd{0} ok, \cmd{1} the self-check or \cmd{--check} found a problem, \cmd{2} bad usage or unreadable file. Bad XML stops with \cmd{file:line: message}.}\par
\head{Becomes a TODO (finish by hand)}
\begin{itemize}
\item Diagrams and layout (redraw v2 views from the text).
\item State machines, interactions, operations; decision, merge, fork, join nodes, object flows, pins.
\item OCL and opaque constraints (the expression is kept); constraint blocks (empty \cmd{constraint def}); parametrics beyond plain binding.
\item Stereotypes outside SysML 1.x (company profiles, UAF, MARTE).
\item Units: specialize the ISQ quantity by hand. DOORS images become \cmd{[image]}; tables flatten to \cmd{a | b}.
\end{itemize}
\head{Git for the port}
\begin{itemize}
\item One branch per segment: \cmd{git switch -c port/<segment>}; merge through the gate (lint 0/0, then review).
\item Stage by hunk, \cmd{git add -p}, so a re-run cannot slip unreviewed changes in.
\item Commit the export's date in the message; tag a baseline every four weeks (\cmd{git tag -a baseline-N}).
\item Undo a bad conversion before commit: \cmd{git restore model/<segment>}.
\end{itemize}
\end{multicols}

{\sffamily\bfseries\LARGE Mapping, exports and checks}\hfill{\sffamily\large quick reference}\par\vspace{3pt}
\hrule height 1.2pt\vspace{2pt}
\begin{multicols}{2}
\head{What maps to what}
{\footnotesize\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.12}\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.41\linewidth} >{\ttfamily\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
SysML v1 (XMI) & \normalfont SysML v2 text\\
\midrule
Package (top level) & package (one file)\\
Block, Class, Component, Actor & part def; generalization :>\\
InterfaceBlock (or port-only Class) & port def; FlowProperty in/out item\\
Part property (composite) & part n : T[m..n];\\
Reference property; value property & ref part; attribute (with default)\\
ValueType, DataType; Enumeration & attribute def (unit as comment); enum def\\
Signal & item def\\
Port, Proxy, Full, Flow port & port n : [\textasciitilde]PortDef;\\
Connector; BindingConnector & connect a.p to b.q; bind a = b;\\
Activity & action def; first a then b;\\
Requirement (and Cameo kinds) & requirement \{ doorsId, title, verificationMethod \}\\
Satisfy & satisfy R by X;\\
Verify, TestCase & verification def \{ objective \{ verify R; \} \}\\
DeriveReqt & \#derivation connection\\
Trace, Refine, Copy, Dependency; Allocate & dependency from A to B; allocate A to B;\\
Comment & doc /* ... */\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}}
\vspace{2pt}{\small Requirements are named from their id (\cmd{CD-101} \textrightarrow{} \cmd{CD\_101}) by both tools, so links written by one resolve against the other. Names that are not plain identifiers or are v2 reserved words are quoted: \cmd{'serial number'}.}\par
\head{A SysML v2 sample (parses clean)}
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\scriptsize,frame=single,framesep=3pt]
package Sample {
    private import ScalarValues::*;
    port def TrackPort { out attribute track : String; }
    part def Seeker { port out1 : TrackPort; }
    part def Guidance { port in1 : ~TrackPort; }
    part def KillVehicle {
        attribute massKg : Real = 25.0;
        part seeker : Seeker;
        part guidance : Guidance;
        connect seeker.out1 to guidance.in1;
    }
    requirement sysR101 {
        attribute doorsId = "SYS-101";
        doc /* Track the threat. */
    }
    satisfy sysR101 by KillVehicle;
    verification def FlightTest { objective { verify sysR101; } }
}
\end{Verbatim}
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\head{Exporting from Cameo / MagicDraw}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{File > Export To > Eclipse UML2 (v5.x) XMI File} (19.0+, 2021x--2024x). Older MagicDraw: \emph{UML 2.1 XMI File}. Not the native \cmd{.mdzip}.
\item \textbf{Include stereotype applications}, or Blocks come out as plain Classes and requirements lose id and text.
\item \textbf{Used projects}: export libraries (e.g.\ SI value types) with the model, or fix those types by hand. Primitives map to \cmd{ScalarValues::*}.
\item Several files may come out: give the converter the one with \cmd{<uml:Model>}. Diagrams are counted and skipped.
\end{itemize}
\end{minipage}
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\head{Exporting from DOORS}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{ReqIF} (preferred): DOORS 9 \emph{File > Export > ReqIF}; DOORS Next \emph{Export > ReqIF}. A \cmd{.reqifz} is read directly.
\item Include \textbf{Object Heading, Object Text, the absolute number} and the verification-method attribute; add the prefix back with \cmd{--id-prefix SYS-}.
\item \textbf{CSV} fallback: Object Identifier, Object Level, Object Heading, Object Text, Verification Method (found by name; others with \cmd{--col}).
\item Heading only \textrightarrow{} a package (section); text \textrightarrow{} a requirement; neither \textrightarrow{} a counted TODO.
\end{itemize}
\end{minipage}
\head{Checking the output}
\begin{itemize}
\item Every run self-checks: balanced braces, strings and comments; every type, target, connect end and import resolves (by name, not scope).
\item \cmd{--check} adds the grammar check: \cmd{perl tools/sysml/sysml.pl check FILE...} (Vim: \cmd{\textbackslash mx}).
\item \cmd{perl tools/sysml/model.pl lint} and \cmd{check} (outline rule, level tags) on the whole model (Vim: \cmd{\textbackslash ml}, \cmd{\textbackslash mk}).
\item Not a full semantic validator: open a segment in a SysML v2 tool before you baseline it, when you can.
\end{itemize}
\head{How the port feeds A--Z}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{A}: \cmd{status-metrics.pl init --xmi} freezes the denominator with \cmd{uml:(Class|Port|Property|Connector|Activity)}; the report's \emph{ported vs remaining} counts the same set.
\item \textbf{C, F, G, I}: \cmd{reqif2sysml.pl --report --model model export.reqif}: linked, orphans, unverified, trace \%, with the ids for the owners.
\item Commit the default \cmd{--req-style usage}: it is the form the collector counts.
\end{itemize}
\vspace{2pt}{\small Full guide: \cmd{docs/SYSML-PORT.html}; help: \cmd{perl agile.pl help xmi2sysml}; the worked model: \cmd{examples/halberd/}.}\par
\end{multicols}
